title: Chapter 9: Weathering, Mass Wasting and Erosion

blocks.content: Weathering, mass wasting, and erosion are the three interconnected geomorphic processes that shape the Earth's surface. Weathering weakens rocks, mass wasting moves material downslope under gravity, and erosion removes and transports sediments through external agents such as water, wind, glaciers, and waves. Together, they control landscape evolution and sedimentary cycles.
Weathering, mass wasting, and erosion are the three interconnected geomorphic processes that shape the Earth's surface.

items: Mass wasting is distinct because it is primarily driven by gravity rather than external transporting agents.
Erosion relies on four specific external agents: water, wind, glaciers, and waves.
Questions often test the distinction between weathering (rock weakening) and erosion (sediment removal and transport).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Weathering, mass wasting, and erosion work together as the three core geomorphic processes shaping the Earth's surface.
Weathering acts to weaken intact rock structures.
Mass wasting transfers weathered material downslope under the direct influence of gravity.
Erosion removes and transports sediments across landscapes via external agents including water, wind, glaciers, and waves.
These combined processes control overall landscape evolution and drive global sedimentary cycles.
